races.title: State Assembly, District 67
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Mark Pulido
cands.bio: Cerritos City Councilmember and Mayor Pro Tempore, with service on the council from 2011 to 2020 and again since 2025. He was ABC Unified School Board member from 2001 to 2011, and earlier worked as a district director and legislative consultant. Democrat.

endorsements.text: California Teachers Association and California Environmental Voters (listed on Ballotpedia).

His campaign site lists endorsements from many labor unions, the Association of Orange County Deputy Sheriffs, California Medical Association, Attorney General Rob Bonta, Treasurer Fiona Ma, Rep. Judy Chu, and many current and former Assembly members.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Pulido on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth limits, H-1B or immigration enforcement, campaign donor pledges, gun laws, abortion, or school choice. His campaign site speaks only in general terms of better schools, safer communities, affordable housing and lower costs for working families. The campaign site describes his city record, such as a 35% drop in burglaries and approval of business developments, but we found no independent source confirming those claims. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey. We read no news reports on him, so we cannot say whether any controversies exist.

local.label: Roots 100: Wikipedia says he was born in Norwalk, CA and moved to Cerritos in 1973, where he attended Whitney High School. His campaign site calls him a 54-year Cerritos resident who attended local schools.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Cerritos City Council member (2011–2020, 2025–present) and mayor, ABC Unified School Board member for three terms (2001–2011), district director for Rep. Alan Lowenthal, and legislative consultant to Robert Hertzberg, Herb Wesson and Fabian Núñez. He holds a master's degree in public policy.
qual.why: Long local elected service plus legislative staff and policy experience puts him in the middle-to-upper range. He has not served in a state legislature.

cands.name: Paulo Morales
cands.bio: Retired Cypress Police Department officer with more than two decades of service, including patrol, detective work and SWAT. Former president of the Cypress Police Officers Association and of the MADD Orange County board. Republican candidate for California Assembly District 67 in 2026.

endorsements.text: The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn (voter guide recommendation)
April's Common Sense Cali Voters and Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide (voter guide recommendations)

cands.gaps: His birthplace is not stated in any page we read. We found no documented actions in office, since he has not held elective office. We found no statements from him on data centers, homestead property taxes, foreign or institutional land buyers, immigration or H-1B, guns, or abortion. He did not complete the Ballotpedia candidate survey. His campaign site does not give specific dates or years for his police career, and we found no independent reporting confirming his biography. No news coverage or controversies were found in the pages provided.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says families should have meaningful choices, including public and private options, so that resources follow the student.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says he supports responsible development and wants to reform the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), which he says is often used to stall housing, and to streamline approvals.

back-police-order.evidence: Says he will insist on clear, enforceable, fully funded laws that give officers the tools and training they need, and wants policies that reduce violent crime and address repeat offenders.
